rationale.Hydroxyurea: Stimulates fetal hemoglobin (HbF) production — improves symptoms long-term.
rationale.IV Ceftriaxone / Cefotaxime (CAP treatme: Community-acquired pneumonia — IV cephalosporin. Blood culture shows H. influenzae B.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a 6-year-old boy with previously undiagnosed sickle cell disease (HbSS) who presents with generalized body pain, fever, and respiratory distress consistent with acute vaso-occlusive crisis complicated by acute chest syndrome and lobar pneumonia (H. influenzae B). CBC shows anemia. Peripheral smear demonstrates sickled cells. Hemoglobin electrophoresis is REQUIRED for definitive diagnosis — it differentiates HbSS from other thalassemias. Sickle cell disease is autosomal recessive: single amino acid substitution (valine for glutamic acid) on beta-globin chain → HbS. Does not present before 6 months due to protective HbF. Patients are functionally asplenic by age 8 from repeated splenic infarction → susceptible to encapsulated organisms (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae B, Salmonella). Management: IV fluids (dehydration precipitates sickling), IV opioids (morphine) for severe pain, oxygen for hypoxia, IV ceftriaxone (CAP treatment), blood transfusion if acute chest syndrome with hypoxia unresponsive to O2. Hydroxyurea stimulates HbF production. Penicillin prophylaxis (lifelong if severe infection history). Consult pediatric hematology. Admit to inpatient. Meningococcal vaccine early (asplenia risk).
